Name: Alpha Drone
Concept: Straightforward baseline fight — no gimmick, good early/tutorial boss
AbilityText: No special ability — the control-group boss every other boss is tuned against.
FlavorText: First off the crashed hive-ship and first to find you. It doesn't need a trick — it's still got the whole swarm behind it.

Name: Broodmother
Concept: Spawns an extra minion each round (breeds)
AbilityText: Breeds: 15% chance each round to spawn 1 extra minion at the start of the fight, on top of the location's printed minion count.
FlavorText: Egg sacs ripple under her shell with every step. Kill her fast, or the escort you counted only grows.

Name: Ironshell
Concept: High resistance/armor — needs sustained hits to bring down
AbilityText: Armor Plating: no special ability beyond its higher 8 HP pool — built to take sustained hits.
FlavorText: Generations of impact with the hull plating fused its carapace into something closer to armor than chitin. It brings fewer hands, and doesn't need more.

Name: Sandreaver
Concept: Burrows — buffs minions' range-position targeting priority
AbilityText: Heat-Seeking Burrow: while active, minions have a 30% chance to deal +1 bonus damage when attacking a player in range position. Active only when Sandreaver is drawn at a Desert location; otherwise it fights as a plain 6 HP boss.
FlavorText: Tremors in the dune are the only warning. It reads the heat of a body at a distance and marks the range-fighters first.

Name: Bogfather
Concept: Passively heals each round it's in the swamp
AbilityText: Swamp Regeneration: if still alive when hands run dry, heals 1 HP once before End Phase Combat begins. Active only when Bogfather is drawn at a Swamp location; otherwise it fights as a plain 6 HP boss.
FlavorText: Half-submerged and patient, it drinks the marsh's rot back into its own wounds. Every hand you waste is HP it gets to keep.

Name: Frostclaw
Concept: Slows players — reduces equipment draw or freezes a card in hand
AbilityText: Chill: 40% chance each round to freeze one random player's hand, reducing that player's equipment draw for the round by 1 (minimum 1 card). Active only when Frostclaw is drawn at an Ice/Tundra location; otherwise it fights as a plain 6 HP boss.
FlavorText: Its breath crusts a blade or a bandage in rime before you can use it. The frozen tundra fights on its side.

Name: Vinewarden
Concept: Regenerates HP tied to its jungle terrain bonus
AbilityText: Regrowth: regenerates 1 HP at the end of each of the first 2 combat cycles it survives each round (max +2 HP/round). Active only when Vinewarden is drawn at a Jungle location; otherwise it fights as a plain 6 HP boss.
FlavorText: Root-fused and bark-plated, it draws strength straight from the canopy around it. Every cycle you don't finish it, the jungle patches it back up.

Name: Magmapincer
Concept: Deals burn damage over time to whoever last hit it
AbilityText: Burn: 30% chance each round that the first player to damage Magmapincer that round takes 1 unblockable burn damage. Active only when Magmapincer is drawn at a Volcanic/Caves location; otherwise it fights as a plain 6 HP boss.
FlavorText: Its shell runs hotter than the caldera it nests in. Land the first hit and you might carry an ember home with you.

Name: Wreckstalker
Concept: Ambush — shifts crab targeting priority in its favor
AbilityText: Ambush: each of Wreckstalker's own attacks has a 25% chance to target the round's first player directly, ignoring the normal melee/range priority order. Active only when Wreckstalker is drawn at a Ruins/Wreckage location; otherwise it fights as a plain 6 HP boss.
FlavorText: It knows the wreckage better than the crew does, and it knows exactly which of you called the shots this round.

Name: Tideshell
Concept: Splits into a minion copy when it takes heavy damage
AbilityText: Split: the first time it takes a tier-2 weapon hit each round, 40% chance to immediately spawn 1 extra minion. Active only when Tideshell is drawn at a Coastal/Reef location; otherwise it fights as a plain 6 HP boss.
FlavorText: A hard enough hit doesn't kill it — it just shakes loose a chunk of itself, hungry and still moving.
